dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: This round of fieldwork has really been a headache...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: ...Hello there. Odd to see you not busy for once. Have you come to chat?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I've been in a bit of a rush recently, so I've barely had the chance to get a few lines in.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Really, it's quite a surprise meeting you here in Ritou. Well, strictly speaking, maybe not. We are all outlanders in the Inazumans' eyes, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Before they get a Residence Permit, all outlanders must remain in Ritou. All that considered, I suppose meeting you here isn't so much of a surprise after all.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: In any case, I'm still waiting for the Outlander Affairs Agency to review and approve my application for a Residence Permit, so I can't leave at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I have been waiting for a while now, though. I wonder when the approval will come down.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Each day spent here is another day's worth of expenses expended and research left undone. Most frustrating indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: So far, I've only been able to ask someone to help me find some "ways and means" to go to other Inazuman islands and conduct some preliminary research.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: What about you? Since you've been able to go to Tsurumi Island, I suppose that your Residence Permit has been processed, right?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Might you have ideas as to how to speed that up, by the way?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I took a backdoor, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Ah, to think that you'd have such connections. Well, for someone like me who lacks them, even getting that permit done is quite the strenuous effort.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Since you had a contact, I suppose that the Outlander Affairs Agency didn't charge you a processing fee either, then?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: When I went to get my documents processed, I specially mentioned that I was a registered researcher with the Akademiya, to be distinguished, of course, from folklorists or other such academic hobbyists.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Only then did the inspector waive some of the fees. Even so, this is a rather troubling process...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Ways and means"?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Huh, it seems that you're not aware.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Well, since we're partners here, I suppose I could tell you. But don't spread it around, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Now, there's a certain fellow here in Ritou named Harrison. He's an outlander too, just like us, and he has his ways.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: If you wish to go somewhere else "on the quiet," you can look for a way near Harrison's store.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: That's all I can say. You'll have to find the way yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: And don't get caught by the Shogunate's people, alright? And if you do, don't mention me.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I don't have the Mora on me to pay any fines.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's your research going?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Smoothly enough, I suppose. Before arriving at Ritou, my previous research topic was "The Practical Uses of the Energy Amplifier."

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Although things went wrong and our research sample was destroyed, we were able to rescue the situation by recovering some sample data.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I have you to thank for that save, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: No need to be so humble. I would never have been able to wrangle with those monsters who had stolen those samples.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: With that data on hand, I reorganized my research into a report that tackled the problem of "how to use the Energy Amplifier to conduct energy conversions."

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: The Akademiya rated my report quite highly. I believe that they must recognized the academic value of this line of inquiry.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I even daresay that this research has filled in a large gap in our understanding of the Energy Amplifier.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: It is of great comfort to me that its value was finally recognized by my seniors in the academic world.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: With that under my belt, I can be said to have graduated successfully. I will not stop here, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I've applied to look into a new research topic. I believe that as long as I keep working at it, I will receive the requisite acknowledgment for that work.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: One day, I will make Dastur... maybe even Herbad!

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: And that's why I'm here in Inazuma, of course, to work on this new topic. It's just a shame that I got stranded here on Ritou before I could make any headway...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dastur?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Oh, that? It's an honorific we use for researchers. Unfortunately, I do not yet have the qualifications to be a Dastur.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I'm still an ordinary traveling scholar from the Aramati, so I'm often sent out to conduct filed research.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: If I make Dastur, then I might be able to stay at the Akademiya more often.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: And when that time comes, I might be able to join such luminaries as the great Pursina and the sagacious Ayesha, and bestow my name upon the fruits of my research, to be used by future generations...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All the best, then. See you!

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: All the best to you too!

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Let's just hope this goes smoothly...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wouldn't call that previous incident easy either.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: That is true. Indeed, it was a most close shave, what with the monsters having made off with the fragments of our sample, after all. I doubt that I would've been able to collect any data by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: With that data on hand, I reorganized my research into a report that tackled the problem of "how to use the Energy Amplifier to conduct energy conversions."

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: The Akademiya rated my report quite highly. I believe that they must recognized the academic value of this line of inquiry.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I even daresay that this research has filled in a large gap in our understanding of the Energy Amplifier.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: It is of great comfort to me that its value was finally recognized by my seniors in the academic world.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: With that under my belt, I can be said to have graduated successfully. I will not stop here, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: I've applied to look into a new research topic. I believe that as long as I keep working at it, I will receive the requisite acknowledgment for that work.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: One day, I will make Dastur... maybe even Herbad!

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: And that's why I'm here in Inazuma, of course, to work on this new topic. It's just a shame that I got stranded here on Ritou before I could make any headway...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Herbad?

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Ah, that is an honorific we use for researchers. Those who earn the name Herbad are knowledgeable beyond the pale, leaders among scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: In my department, the number of great talents who study alchemy and the function of the ley lines are many indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: By contrast, I am not their equal in talent. Truly, I wonder if I can ascend to such heights within my lifetime...

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: But if I can, then perhaps I might be able to join such luminaries as the great Pursina and the sagacious Ayesha, and bestow my name upon the fruits of my research, to be used by future generations...

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: And there will be Hosseini Machines, Hosseini Methods, and Hosseini Formulas used throughout the scholarly realms of Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Hosseini
dialogues.text: Ah, just thinking about it makes my soul sing!
